blocks.text: This page tracks the Ladner MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $1,023,500 for a typical home, down 6.5% over twelve months.
Ladner benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Ladner home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,023,500 in October 2026. That is little changed at −1.0% on the month, down 5.8% over three months, down 4.8% over six months and down 6.5% over the year. Over three years it is down 11.4%, and over five years down 2.6%.
The weakest one-year move in Ladner was for a townhouse homes at −10.2%; the strongest was a detached home at −4.3%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,262,500) and an apartment ($620,000) is $642,500, and a townhouse ($909,300) sits $289,300 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Ladner is 4.2% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 6.5% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Ladner ranks 9 by all-home benchmark, with Squamish above it at $1,100,500 and Richmond below it at $998,300.

Detached homes in Ladner: benchmark $1,262,500, down 1.7% in a month, down 5.1% in three months, down 3.2% in six months, down 4.3% in a year, down 10.1% in three years and down 3.3% in five. That is 28.9% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Ladner: benchmark $909,300, little changed at −1.1% in a month, down 7.0% in three months, down 7.6% in six months, down 10.2% in a year, down 10.8% in three years and up 3.9% in five. That is 9.7% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Ladner: benchmark $620,000, up 5.7% in a month, little changed at +0.0% in three months, little changed at −1.1% in six months, down 5.6% in a year, down 12.4% in three years and little changed at −0.8% in five. That is 7.9% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Ladner home is worth about $71,200 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,094,700. By type, detached homes lost about $56,700, from $1,319,200 to $1,262,500, townhouses lost about $103,300, from $1,012,600 to $909,300, and apartments lost about $36,800, from $656,800 to $620,000 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,075,100 six months ago and near $1,155,200 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $51,600 below the six-month mark and about $131,700 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Ladner benchmark is about $45,100 below the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $32,500 below.
Ladner sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 125 Ladner houses sold at a median of $1.33M (middle half $1.15M to $1.54M), half of them within 21 days. 55 condos sold at a median of $597,500 (middle half $487,500 to $655,350), half within 30 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.26M to $1.23M between November–January and August–October (17 and 18 sales).

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Ladner?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Ladner home was $1,023,500, with detached at $1,262,500.

faq.q: Are Ladner home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Ladner is down 6.5% over twelve months and down 5.8% over three months.
